q: How do I make Revolution play back at a lower resolution automatically when my laptop is unplugged?
a:
1. Choose Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ **Playback…** (`app.settings.playback`).
2. Turn on **Lower playback resolution on battery**.
3. Press **OK**.

While the computer runs on battery, playback now renders one Playback Resolution step lower (Full becomes 1/2). When playback is stopped, and in every export, full resolution is kept. Plugged in again, it returns to your setting within about ten seconds.

q: Is the battery playback setting turned on out of the box?
a: No. Preferences ▸ Playback ▸ **Lower playback resolution on battery** is off by default, so playback keeps your Playback Resolution on battery too until you turn it on.

q: Why is playback suddenly at half resolution since I pulled the charger out?
a: Most likely **Lower playback resolution on battery** is on (Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ Playback, `app.settings.playback`). On battery it plays one Playback Resolution step lower, so Full becomes 1/2. A paused frame and every export stay at full resolution, and plugging in again brings playback back to your setting within about ten seconds. Turn the option off if you'd rather keep full detail on battery.

q: Should I turn on lower playback resolution on battery, or leave it off?
a:
It's a trade-off, not a rule:

- **On:** less detail while playing, in exchange for less heat and a longer battery. A good fit if you cut unplugged (judging timing and story doesn't need full detail) and check detail later.
- **Off (default):** full Playback Resolution on battery too, for when you're judging focus, noise or a grade away from the charger and accept the shorter battery.

Either way, a paused frame and exports are at full resolution. The switch is Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ Playback ▸ **Lower playback resolution on battery**.

q: What does 'Decoded frames in GPU memory (0 = Auto)' pick on a laptop with only integrated graphics?
a: That setting (Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ **Memory…**, `app.settings.memory`,) is how much graphics memory keeps recently decoded frames, so scrubbing back and forth doesn't decode again. An integrated GPU has no memory of its own; it shares the computer's RAM, so on Auto (0) Revolution sizes it from that shared RAM: an eighth of it, at most 4 GB. Type a number of MB to override it.

q: how do i give filmcraft more memory for scrubbing on my intel igpu
a:
1. Choose Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ **Memory…** (`app.settings.memory`).
2. Set **Decoded frames in GPU memory** to the number of MB you want (0 = Auto).
3. Press **OK**.

On an integrated GPU, Auto uses an eighth of the RAM it shares, at most 4 GB. A larger number keeps more recently decoded frames, so scrubbing back and forth decodes again less often; the memory comes out of the same RAM the rest of the computer uses, so leave room for other programs. The same dialog's **Decoded source frames** does the same for frames held in main memory.

q: Will my laptop go to sleep in the middle of a long render?
a: Revolution asks the desktop not to suspend while an export runs, so the idle sleep timer shouldn't stop it. The laptop's lid setting may still suspend it, though: if closing the lid suspends your laptop, keep it open (or change the lid setting in your desktop's power settings) while the export runs.

q: Does Revolution have anything like dropping preview quality when running on battery power?
a: Yes, as a fork option: Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ Playback ▸ **Lower playback resolution on battery**, off by default. On battery it renders playback one Playback Resolution step lower; stopped frames and exports stay full resolution. For a longer battery you can also set **Graphics device** in the same dialog to **Power saving (integrated GPU)** (takes effect at the next start), which is quieter and longer on battery but may drop frames with heavy grades or 4K+ effects.
